t1.text: Rain should feel like Oregon: now, then the season

n1.text:
Q2 · How the two stories sit (Matt leans to C)

A (top row). The feature tile under the temperature carries the now story: a dual chart, rain every 5 min as columns and the running total as a line. The hero ends with the wet-hours meter, two bars (7 days, 30 days): the season at a glance on the first screen. Matt likes C, so report C as the lead; A is the earlier recommendation. The Dry spell slot turns into Wet hours in wet mode; "Last rain 9 h ago" is its delta once rain stops leading. Mosaic order and one-link tiles unchanged.

Tap: the feature and the meter both open the rain zoom, which runs now, then season, then usual (Rain tab C). Now → season is one scroll in the zoom; season → now is the same zoom's top.

B. Meter shrinks into the hero's top right; in wet mode the first mosaic row becomes Wet hours | Rain since Oct 1. Breaks the fixed tile order (Mosaic decision 23).

C. One rain tile: now on top, a season strip at its foot. Two links in one tile; the season is on screen only while rain leads.

n2.text: Sample values shaped like Lookout Post on Mon Nov 23, 2026. The 30-day wet hours are the back-test's real days (Oct 25 to Nov 22), plus 3 wet hours today for the rain scenario. Nov 5 is hatched only to show a missing day. Rain since Oct 1: 3.67 in measured + 0.31 in today = 3.98 in, against 7.58 (2026), 10.08 (2025) and 7.90 (2024) by this date: drier.

n3.text:
Flags

1. The meter is now two hour bars, 7 days and 30 days ("19 h of 168", "112 h of 720"), after Matt's comment that hours beat percent. This replaces the decided one track 0–100% with two markers. The Wet hours tile carries the same number: one fact, shown twice.
2. In dry mode the meter hides: it would read 0 h for months. The DryDay board shows the hero without it.
3. Tile order: Wet hours moves up beside Temperature; Rain since Oct 1 moves to row 2. This breaks the fixed tile order (Mosaic decision 23) while it is wet.

n4.text:
Q4 · Recommend C: now, then season, then usual

Principle 1 read literally. The tab opens on a short now band (the last 24 hours by the hour, with last rain), then the season (wet hours each day of the water year, and the wet share by window on one meter), then usual (the water-year curves with the verdict, and each window against its usual range).

The headline becomes the verdict over the curves: "3.98 in · drier than usual". The window strip becomes a dot-on-band chart: each window's rain as a dot on its own usual range, so wetter and drier read at once.

Cost: Mosaic decision 14 made the water year the top section so the rain zoom is a crop of the tab's lead. Under C the rain zoom is the tab's first two sections and the Rain since Oct 1 tile crops the third. A keeps decision 14; B leads with the season calendar.

n5.text:
Q5 · Pick: B + C on one page (Matt: this is the one to pick), the step glyph

B shows the events by size, which Matt finds more telling than the timeline: the sweep of the seasons beats when each event fell. C's list is every event of the water year, newest first, each row opening to its rate and accumulation chart.

A, the timeline, is dropped (Matt: drop this, polish C).

B and C are not either/or by condition: they answer different questions (how big; which and when). The board under them, B + C, puts both on one page: B's scatter unchanged, then C's list with the filter line on it. Matt picked it; every Rain Events link opens it.

Glyph: four steps filled to the category (sprinkle 1, shower 2, rain 3, storm 4). It reads as a size, not a picture, lines up on every row, and draws in one colour. The word stays beside it for the screen reader and the first read.

n6.text:
C · The filter line

Three controls on one line, never wrapped: 2026–27 (the water year, a select), Newest (sort: newest, biggest, longest) and Showers and up (size: all, showers and up, rain and storms). Each pill's accessible name says the whole thing ("Sort: newest first"). A line under the pills says what is shown: "8 events, sprinkles hidden".

The headline is counted from the season, "10 events this water year · 3 in the last 7 days", never from a fixed last 10. A new water year in October then never says "last 10 events" across two seasons. The season is the water year, Oct 1 to Sep 30 (GLOSSARY).
